title: Annotatio II §.III CONCEPTIO: Triple error of consubstantiation-pressers — PRIMUS starts in early Fathers
pass_a_gloss: We judge the CONCEPTION is to be located in a triple error of those who have at length pressed either Consubstantiation. Of these errors the FIRST is discharged by badly understood Sayings of the earliest Fathers, hinting that the sacred Eucharist consists either of two things, that is Substances, earthly and celestial, or of one earthly substance only, yet increased by some Celestial Accident — either of External Holiness or of Intrinsic Divine Virtue.
pass_b_english: CONCEPTION sits in a triple error of those who finally pressed either Consubstantiation.

FIRST error: early Fathers badly read — as if the Eucharist were two substances (earthly + celestial), or one earthly substance plus some celestial accident of external holiness or intrinsic divine virtue.
source_text: CONCEPTIONEM locandam arbitramur in triplici errore eorum, qui Consubstantiationem alterutram enixi tandèm sunt. Horum errorum PRIMUM absolvunt malè intellecta Patrum primorum Dicta, vel, ex duabus rebus, id est Substantiis, terrena, & cælesti, vel ex una tantum terrena substantia, at Accidente quodam Cælesti, sive Externæ Sanctitatis, sive Virtutis Divinæ Intrinsecæ, adaucta, Eucharistiam sacram constare innuentium.
notes: CONCEPTIO in triple error; PRIMUS = early Fathers.
